official.deadline_central_display: No fellowship deadline: master's application to be completed before 1 December; admission offer before February; nominees informed before 1 February
official.deadline_note: There is no scholarship application deadline: it is not possible to actively apply for an Eric Bleumink Fellowship. Only applicants who have received a provisional or unconditional admission offer for a master's programme before February can be considered, so the master's application should be completed before 1 December.
official.application_cycle: Annual cycle tied to master's admission for a September start; master's application completed before 1 December for the following September intake
official.status_note: The Board of the Eric Bleumink Fellowship selects new recipients each year; candidates are nominated from applicants already admitted to a University of Groningen master's programme, so there is no separate application window.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The grant covers tuition fee, costs of international travel, subsistence, books, and health insurance.
benefits: Living allowance of EUR 1250,00 per month for food and accommodation, paid at the end of the month for the next month
Settling allowance of EUR 275 for extra expenses incurred when arriving in the Netherlands
eligibility: Hold the nationality of a country appearing in Appendix 1 (published list of countries of origin)
Have received provisional or unconditional admission for a master programme before February
Have excellent academic performance, preferably to be confirmed by letters of recommendation, and excellent grades during bachelor/undergraduate studies
Have excellent English language proficiency, in accordance with the admission requirements of the program of choice
Be available for the whole period of the programme and be able to take part in the entire programme, starting 1 September
Be in good health, so that health insurance in the Netherlands can be arranged, and have no other means of financing the study in question
requirements: Master's application completed by the applicant before 1 December
Provisional or unconditional admission offer for a master programme received before February
Copies of application forms for other funding requests submitted (motivation evidence)
documents: The master's programme admission application itself, which forms the basis of the nomination
Letters of recommendation confirming academic performance
Copies of application forms for other funding requests
selection_criteria: The contribution of the candidate's education in terms of strengthening the scientific capacity in the candidate's home country
The perspectives of contribution to long-term links between the university in the developing country and the University of Groningen are preferable
A proper balance between male and female candidates, ranging over various disciplines (faculties) and regional variety over different continents
Motivation: which requests for other funding have also been submitted (copies of application forms)
Any other scholarship offered by the University of Groningen simultaneously with the EBF Talent Grant is not allowed
coverage: Subsistence (living allowance of EUR 1250,00 per month for food and accommodation)
Settling allowance of EUR 275 and train travel (2nd class fare) between Amsterdam Airport Schiphol and Groningen
application_method: Apply for admission to a University of Groningen master's programme through the normal admission route
No separate scholarship application: the Admission Office, in consultation with the Admission Boards of the faculties, determines which applicants are nominated
Nominated candidates are informed before 1 February; if the Admission Office does not make contact, the applicant was not selected
official.application_route: No direct application - complete a University of Groningen master's application before 1 December and hold an admission offer before February; the Admission Office nominates and the EBF Board decides
official.citizenship_residency: Hold the nationality of a country appearing in Appendix 1 of the fellowship's published country-of-origin list
official.international_eligibility: Only nationals of the countries listed in Appendix 1 are eligible; all listed countries are outside the Netherlands
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: None - all master's programmes (MSc/MA/LL.M.) are eligible, although the selection committee balances disciplines and regions
official.duration: 1 year or 2 years Master's degree programme, starting in September only
official.description: The funds raised by the Eric Bleumink Fellowship are made available with the intention of providing grants to students from the least developed countries: promising students who wish to obtain a Master's degree and may be invited to study at the University of Groningen. The training of the candidates should make a contribution to increasing the academic capability of the country in question.
official.program_type: Master's scholarship grant (MSc/MA/LL.M.) awarded by the University of Groningen, nomination-based
official.english_requirement: Excellent English language proficiency, in accordance with the admission requirements of the program of choice

applicant_utility.summary: This is a nomination-only award: there is no fellowship form to submit, so the only date that matters is 1 December, when your University of Groningen master's application must already be complete so the Admission Office can nominate you once you hold an offer. The money arrives as a package rather than a lump sum - tuition, books, health insurance and international travel are paid, and you receive EUR 1250 per month for food and accommodation plus a EUR 275 settling allowance on arrival. With hundreds of eligible applicants each year and the fund's own rules noting only a handful of grants, treat admission to the right master's programme, not the fellowship form, as your real application.
applicant_utility.best_fit: A top-graded bachelor graduate from an Appendix 1 country targeting a one- or two-year Groningen master's with a September start and no other funding in place.
application_readiness_checklist: Finish the master's application (Studielink plus the UG portal) before 1 December - a late file never reaches the nomination pool
Check your nationality against the published Appendix 1 country list before investing time and money in the application
Secure strong, specific reference letters early, since recommendation letters are the preferred proof of academic performance
Monitor your admission status so you hold a provisional or unconditional offer before February
Keep copies of every other funding application you submit, as the motivation review asks for them
Route questions to the Mobility and Scholarship Desk (msd@rug.nl); the fund explicitly asks applicants not to send fellowship applications
common_rejection_risks: Missing the 1 December master's cut-off, which silently removes you from nomination even with excellent grades
Aiming at a February or April start - the grant is only awarded for programmes starting in September
Holding another University of Groningen scholarship at the same time, which the rules prohibit
Assuming silence means pending: if you are not contacted before 1 February, you were not selected
Being seen to have other means of financing, which breaches the 'no other means of financing' criterion
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Residence permit/MVV and visa costs, personal and leisure spending beyond the subsistence allowance, and any costs of accompanying family members.
document_audit: There are no fellowship-specific documents; nomination rests on your master's admission file, so any gap there (missing transcript, weak motivation letter) is also a fellowship gap
Reference letters must be specific enough to evidence 'excellent academic performance' - generic letters undercut the top selection criterion
Other funding application forms must be copy-ready, since motivation is judged partly on which alternative funding you pursued
alerts: Nominees are informed before 1 February and decisions of the EBF Board cannot be appealed
The fund's regulations state that hundreds of applications arrive each year but only a few grants are awarded
The award follows a September-start programme only, so a delayed or alternative-start offer disqualifies the funding
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: You apply only for the master's programme; the Admissions Office and faculty Admission Boards nominate, the EBF Board decides, and nominees hear before 1 February.
